chunks: And from him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman Al-Azramy, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever mentions the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the beginning of food or drink, and praises Allah at its end, will not be questioned about the blessing of that food ever.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for saying Bismillah and Al-Hamdulillah during meals?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) links the ritual of Bismillah and Al-Hamdulillah to the eschatological concept of 'Hasb al-Ni'mah' (sufficiency of blessing), where the act itself serves as a complete witness to the divine favor, thereby exempting the believer from detailed accounting. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that mindful gratitude transforms mundane consumption into an act of worship, securing spiritual protection from the scrutiny of one's blessings on the Day of Judgment.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from his father, from the one who narrated it, from Abdul Rahman Al Azramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘

The one who mentioned Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic during a meal, or drink, at the beginning of it, and Praises Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during its end, would not be Questioned about that Bounty of the meal, ever!’
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from those who narrated to him from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-‘Arzamiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘
One who mentions the name of Allah on food or drink at the beginning and ‘All praise belongs to Allah’ at the end, he will never be asked about the blessings of the food.’”
